title: Expand benchmark harness for heterogeneous kernel fuzzing and latency-slice orchestration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current benchmark harness covers canonical mixes and single-kernel golden runs but misses realistic heterogeneous mixes (multiple kernel paths, quantized kernels, and fallback slow paths). CI gates are brittle because thresholds are absolute and don't account for distributional shifts (sequence length mix, token distributions, or noise from host scheduler). Prefill/decode co-scheduling behavior under mixed-tenancy is under-represented, leading to surprises in tail latency.

Goal: Extend the harness to (1) generate and run heterogeneous-kernel fuzz mixes that exercise multiple kernel codepaths in one run, (2) define latency-sliced golden baselines (sequence-length buckets + busy/idle host noise levels), and (3) replace brittle CI thresholds with statistical perf gates (bootstrap-based anomalies) plus a small auto-rebaseline flow for non-customer-impacting noise.

Scope and approach:
- Heterogeneous kernel fuzzing: implement a generator that composes synthetic request traces with probabilistic kernel-path annotations (e.g., 40% fast-fprop, 30% quantized-fprop, 20% kernel-fallback, 10% attention-optimized path). The generator will produce deterministic seeds and a replay harness so CI failures are reproducible.
- Latency-slice orchestration: define canonical buckets (<=64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024 tokens) and per-bucket golden baselines stored as statistical summaries (median, 50/90/99 quantiles, sample variance). Runs will instrument KV cache hit/miss rates and batch occupancy.
- Prefill/decode co-scheduling: simulate multi-tenant prefill-heavy and decode-heavy mixes in the same run to observe KV cache pressure and prefill-decode switching overhead. Add workload scenarios that pin prefill:decode ratios (e.g., 80:20, 50:50, 20:80).
- CI perf gates: implement bootstrap test comparing new run distribution to golden baseline distribution, compute effect size and p-value; fail CI only if probability of regression > 99.5% and observed regression exceeds minimal meaningful effect size (configurable by bucket). Include an auto-rebaseline path for infra-noise-induced non-customer-impacting drift (with reviewer approval recorded).

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We accept longer CI run times for these suites in exchange for much higher signal-to-noise and fewer spurious rollbacks. To keep CI latency acceptable, we will (A) run lightweight smoke versions on each PR and full statistical suites nightly, and (B) allow developers to opt into full runs when changing kernel routing or scheduling code.
- Maintaining deterministic seeds vs. realism: seeds are deterministic but generators will be parameterized by a small set of randomized seeds to avoid overfitting to single traces.

Outcomes and metrics:
- Reduce flaky CI perf failures from kernel-routing changes by 70% within first month of adoption.
- Detect 95% of regressions with effect size >= 5% median increase in tokens/sec in targeted buckets.
- Produce dashboard panels with per-bucket PCR (probability of change/regression) and per-kernel coverage heatmaps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Heterogeneous kernel generator checked into repo and docs explaining seed format.
- Latency-sliced golden baseline storage and retrieval implemented; baselines exported to Grafana-backed dashboard.
- CI jobs configured: PR-level smoke tests + nightly statistical suite. CI fails only under configured statistical conditions.
- Prefill/decode co-schedule scenarios added to canonical workload library and exercised in nightly runs.
- Run artifacts (trace files, summaries) uploaded to S3 and linked in run metadata.

Risks and mitigations:
- Nightly runs may increase cloud costs: mitigate by downsampling and using reserved CI GPUs for bench runs.
- Statistical gate complexity may confuse devs: provide clear docs, examples, and an auto-rebaseline review flow in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Generator and replay harness committed with deterministic seed format and README
Golden baseline per-sequence-length-bucket exists and is queryable via bench CLI
PR-level smoke CI job added; nightly statistical suite job added to pipeline
Bootstrap-based CI gate implemented with configurable effect-size and p-value thresholds
Prefill/decode multi-tenant scenarios added to canonical workload library
Dashboards show per-bucket median/quantile and kernel-coverage heatmaps
